title: Collateral qualifies as peg-stabilizing by the price it commits to, not by what asset it is
content:
A.3.3.2.2.1.1 defines Resting Actively Stabilizing Collateral by an obligation rather than by identity: it "must provide buy support at a price of at least 0.999 USD per USDS (10bps downside spread)." A.3.3.2.3.1 mirrors it on the other side — the Demand Absorption Buffer is USDS "that is for sale for at most 1.001 USD per USDS."

The definition is functional, and the eligible-asset list follows from it rather than the other way round: Resting ASC "includes Cash Stablecoins in PSMs or decentralized exchanges (e.g., Curve), other stablecoins, crypto assets, or off-chain Real World Asset (RWA) loans to market makers, **provided they meet the specified redemption price and transparency requirements**." An offchain loan to a market maker can count as peg-defending collateral if it is genuinely callable at that price; a nominally liquid onchain asset cannot if it is not.

The 10bps band is what makes the commitment meaningful. Capital sitting in a pool that only bids at 0.99 does not defend the peg — it defines a new one. By fixing the price at which support must exist, Sky is specifying the *width of the corridor* it is willing to let USDS trade in, and the ASC requirement is simply how much depth stands at the corridor's edge.

The symmetry of 0.999 / 1.001 gives USDS a stated 20bps two-sided band, which the Peg Defense Event trigger then reuses: A.3.3.2.4.1 declares an emergency when the average price "falls below 0.999 USD per USDS" — the same number as the ASC bid. The routine obligation and the emergency trigger are the same line, so a Peg Defense Event is by definition the moment the resting bids failed to hold.
description: Resting ASC must provide buy support at 0.999 USD per USDS or better (10bps downside spread), and DAB must be offered at no more than 1.001 — a spread commitment any asset class can meet.
